sections.title: DEFINITIONS
sections.summary: This page is a glossary of definitions titled 'DEFINITIONS' from a corporate document, likely an annual report or proxy statement. It lists various acronyms and terms (such as ASC 718, GAAP, NEOs, PSU) alongside their specific meanings in the context of NVIDIA Corporation's compensation plans and governance. The page also references specific documents like the Form 10-K for Fiscal 2026 and regulations such as Regulation S-K.

sections.title: BUSINESS OVERVIEW
sections.summary: The 'BUSINESS OVERVIEW' section details NVIDIA's strong financial performance in Fiscal 2026, highlighting a 65% year-on-year revenue increase to $215.9 billion driven by the Compute & Networking segment and the Blackwell platform. It breaks down results into reportable segments ('Compute & Networking' and 'Graphics') and market platforms ('Data Center', 'Gaming', 'Professional Visualization', and 'Automotive'), providing specific revenue figures and growth percentages for each.

children.title: 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders
children.summary: This section outlines the logistical details for the 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, including the date (Wednesday, June 24, 2026), time (9:00 a.m. Pacific Time), location (virtual at www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/NVDA2026), record date (April 27, 2026), and admission requirements (Control Number).

children.title: Voting Matters and Board Recommendations
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Voting Matters and Board Recommendations
children.summary: This section outlines the Board of Directors' recommendations for the 2026 Annual Meeting proposals. It categorizes seven items into Management Proposals (1-3) and Stockholder Proposals (4-7). The Board recommends voting FOR the election of directors, advisory approval of executive compensation, and ratification of PwC as the independent auditor. Conversely, the Board recommends voting AGAINST four stockholder proposals regarding a simple majority vote standard, reports on faith-based community resource groups, workforce civil liberties, and greenhouse gas emissions disclosure. The table details the specific vote required for approval and the effect of abstentions or broker non-votes for each matter.

children.title: Election of Directors (Proposal 1)
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Election of Directors (Proposal 1)
children.summary: This page details the 'Election of Directors (Proposal 1)' and provides a summary table of director nominees including their age, tenure, independence status, and committee memberships. It includes a recommendation to vote for each nominee and discusses recent board refreshment, specifically mentioning the appointment of Suzanne Nora Johnson effective July 13, 2026. The bottom section outlines key skills and competencies required for directors and maps these attributes against specific nominees like Coxe, Huang, and Hudson.

children.title: Corporate Governance Highlights
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Corporate Governance Highlights
children.summary: The section outlines the company's commitment to strong corporate governance and its collaborative approach with stockholders. It details key governance practices, including having an independent Lead Director, declassified board, majority voting for directors, and active oversight of risk management. The text also highlights director attendance requirements, self-assessments, and stock ownership guidelines.

children.title: Advisory Approval of Executive Compensation for Fiscal 2026 (Proposal 2)
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Advisory Approval of Executive Compensation for Fiscal 2026 (Proposal 2)

children.title: Executive Compensation Highlights
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Advisory Approval of Executive Compensation for Fiscal 2026 (Proposal 2)/Executive Compensation Highlights
children.summary: This section outlines the company's executive compensation philosophy, emphasizing a performance-based and at-risk structure designed to align NEO interests with stockholders. It details that for Fiscal 2026, cash compensation remained constant while target equity opportunities were increased. The text also describes specific financial goals set by the Compensation Committee (CC) for the Base Compensation Plan, including revenue targets for Variable Cash Plans and operating income targets for PSUs.

children.title: Financial Performance and Link to Executive Pay
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Advisory Approval of Executive Compensation for Fiscal 2026 (Proposal 2)/Financial Performance and Link to Executive Pay
children.summary: This section details the link between financial performance and executive pay for Fiscal 2026. It explains that a significant portion of executive compensation is tied to financial metrics driving business value. The content includes two tables: 'Performance Goals' outlines targets for Variable Cash Plans, SY PSUs, and MY PSUs based on revenue, operating income, and Total Shareholder Return (TSR); and 'Performance Achievement and Payouts' shows the actual results achieved at the end of Fiscal 2026 and the corresponding payout percentages relative to target opportunities.

children.title: Ratification of Selection of PwC as our Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm for Fiscal 2027 (Proposal 3)
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Ratification of Selection of PwC as our Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm for Fiscal 2027 (Proposal 3)
children.summary: This section requests stockholders to ratify the Audit Committee's selection of PwC as the independent registered public accounting firm for Fiscal 2027. It states that while ratification is not required, the Board recommends a 'FOR' vote, noting that the AC may still retain or change the firm regardless of the stockholder vote.

children.title: Stockholder Proposal 4
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Stockholder Proposal 4
children.summary: This section addresses Stockholder Proposal 4, which requests the Board to replace supermajority voting provisions in the Company's Charter and Bylaws with a simple majority standard. The proposal is advisory only. The text notes that at the 2025 Meeting, a similar amendment was proposed but did not pass. Consequently, the Board recommends that stockholders vote AGAINST this proposal.

children.title: Stockholder Proposal 5
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Stockholder Proposal 5
children.summary: Stockholder Proposal 5 requests the Board to evaluate and report on faith-based community resource groups. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating that existing policies, practices, and feedback mechanisms already address these issues.

children.title: Stockholder Proposal 6
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Stockholder Proposal 6
children.summary: Stockholder Proposal 6 requests the Board to evaluate and report on civil rights and non-discrimination related to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI). The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating that NVIDIA complies with applicable law, is committed to equal employment opportunity, and maintains strong oversight mechanisms for these policies.

children.title: Stockholder Proposal 7
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/Stockholder Proposal 7
children.summary: Stockholder Proposal 7 requests that the Board report and disclose greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from the use of NVIDIA's sold products. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating that such disclosure is unnecessary given NVIDIA's existing robust climate reporting history, targets, and future plans. The Board asserts that management is best positioned to determine the specific content and methodology for these disclosures.

children.title: PROXY STATEMENT FOR THE 2026 ANNUAL MEETING OF STOCKHOLDERS - JUNE 24, 2026
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY SUMMARY/PROXY STATEMENT FOR THE 2026 ANNUAL MEETING OF STOCKHOLDERS - JUNE 24, 2026
children.summary: This section provides information regarding the 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders for NVIDIA Corporation, scheduled for June 24, 2026. It details the virtual meeting format, attendance eligibility based on the April 27, 2026 record date, and instructions for voting and asking questions via proxyvote.com or the virtual shareholder meeting website. Additionally, it outlines the quorum requirements, specifying that a majority of outstanding shares must be represented to hold the meeting.

children.title: Information About the 2026 Meeting
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting

children.title: Virtual Meeting Philosophy and Benefits
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Virtual Meeting Philosophy and Benefits
children.summary: This section outlines the Board's rationale for holding the 2026 Meeting in a virtual format, citing benefits such as increased participation regardless of location and reduced costs. It also details measures taken to protect stockholder rights, including opportunities to ask questions, publishing answers on the Investor Relations website, and providing a webcast replay.

children.title: Meeting Attendance
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Meeting Attendance
children.summary: This section outlines the eligibility and procedures for attending the 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. It specifies that stockholders as of the April 27, 2026 record date or those holding a valid proxy may attend virtually at www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/NVDA2026 using their Control Number. The text also notes that anyone can listen to the meeting live, provides technical support contact information, mentions a webcast replay available through June 24, 2027, and recommends voting by proxy even if planning to attend.

children.title: Asking Questions
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Asking Questions
children.summary: This section outlines the process for stockholders to submit questions regarding the 2026 Annual Meeting. It encourages submissions via a pre-meeting forum at www.proxyvote.com and during the meeting at www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/NVDA2026. The company plans to answer as many questions as time permits, group similar questions, and respond to only one question per stockholder to ensure fairness and efficient use of resources. Questions unrelated to company business or unsuitable for the meeting may be excluded.

children.title: Quorum and Voting
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Quorum and Voting
children.summary: The section titled 'Quorum and Voting' explains the requirements for holding the 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. It states that a quorum is achieved when a majority of outstanding shares entitled to vote are represented, either by virtual attendance or proxy. The text specifies the record date as April 27, 2026, notes there were 24,220,525,225 shares outstanding on that date, and calculates that 12,110,262,613 shares must be represented to establish a quorum.

children.title: Stockholder of Record
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Quorum and Voting/Stockholder of Record
children.summary: This section defines a 'Stockholder of Record' as someone whose shares are registered directly with the transfer agent, Computershare, on April 27, 2026. It provides a table outlining five methods for these stockholders to vote, change their vote, or revoke their proxy: virtually attending the meeting, mailing a proxy card, voting by telephone/online, submitting a later proxy card, or sending a written notice of revocation to NVIDIA Corporation.

children.title: Street Name Holder
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Quorum and Voting/Street Name Holder
children.summary: This section explains the voting rights and procedures for beneficial owners of shares held in 'street name' through a nominee, such as a bank or broker. It details that these shareholders must direct their nominee on how to vote and obtain a valid proxy to attend the 2026 Meeting virtually. The text defines 'broker non-votes' which occur when instructions are not provided for non-routine matters like director elections or executive compensation. It emphasizes that specific instructions are mandatory for Proposals 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7 (non-discretionary items) for votes to be counted.

children.title: Vote Count
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Quorum and Voting/Vote Count
children.summary: This section outlines the voting rules for seven proposals at the NVIDIA meeting. It specifies that stockholders have one vote per share as of April 27, 2026. A table details each proposal (including the election of directors and various stockholder proposals), the required vote threshold for approval (typically a majority of shares present or 'More FOR than AGAINST'), and the effect of abstentions and broker non-votes.

children.title: Vote Results
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Quorum and Voting/Vote Results
children.summary: This section states that preliminary voting results will be announced at the 2026 Meeting, while final results will be published in a current report on Form 8-K filed with the SEC by June 30, 2026.

children.title: Proxy Materials
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Proxy Materials
children.summary: This section explains how NVIDIA makes proxy materials available to stockholders online at www.nvidia.com/proxy. It details the distribution of a Notice on or about May 12, 2026, for stockholders of record as of April 27, 2026, providing instructions on accessing materials and voting online or by telephone. The text also describes options for receiving future materials electronically via www.proxyvote.com or www.icsdelivery.com/nvda, and outlines the 'householding' practice where companies deliver a single set of materials to multiple stockholders sharing an address.

children.title: 2027 Meeting Deadlines for Submission of Stockholder Proposals, Nomination of Directors, and Other Business
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/2027 Meeting Deadlines for Submission of Stockholder Proposals, Nomination of Directors, and Other Business

children.title: Proposals to be Considered for Inclusion in Our Proxy Materials Pursuant to Rule 14a-8
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/2027 Meeting Deadlines for Submission of Stockholder Proposals, Nomination of Directors, and Other Business/Proposals to be Considered for Inclusion in Our Proxy Materials Pursuant to Rule 14a-8
children.summary: This section outlines the requirements for stockholders wishing to submit proposals for inclusion in the 2027 Meeting proxy materials pursuant to Rule 14a-8. It specifies that proposals must be submitted in writing or by email to NVIDIA Corporation, addressed to Secretary Timothy S. Teter, with a deadline of January 12, 2027.

children.title: Director Nominations Under Our Proxy Access Bylaw
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/2027 Meeting Deadlines for Submission of Stockholder Proposals, Nomination of Directors, and Other Business/Director Nominations Under Our Proxy Access Bylaw
children.summary: This section outlines the requirements for stockholders to nominate directors under the company's Proxy Access Bylaw. Eligible stockholders (or groups of up to 20) must have owned at least 3% of voting power for three continuous years and can nominate up to two candidates or 20% of the board. The notice period for the 2027 Meeting is specified as between February 24, 2027, and March 26, 2027.

children.title: Other Director Nominations and Proposals
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/2027 Meeting Deadlines for Submission of Stockholder Proposals, Nomination of Directors, and Other Business/Other Director Nominations and Proposals
children.summary: This section outlines the procedures for stockholders to nominate a director or introduce business items at the 2027 annual meeting that are not included in the proxy materials. It specifies that such nominations must be submitted in writing between February 24, 2027, and March 26, 2027. The text also details alternative notice deadlines if the meeting date is delayed or moved more than 30 days from the anniversary of the previous year's meeting.

children.title: Additional Requirements and Information
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/2027 Meeting Deadlines for Submission of Stockholder Proposals, Nomination of Directors, and Other Business/Additional Requirements and Information
children.summary: This section advises stockholders to review the company's Bylaws for additional requirements regarding advance notice of proposals and director nominations. It highlights the Board's commitment to considering feedback on these processes and outlines specific engagement protocols with stockholders proposing amendments that would require disclosure of plans to nominate candidates to other public boards or information about limited partners.

children.title: Proposal 1—Election of Directors
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the 2026 Meeting/Proposal 1—Election of Directors
children.summary: This page outlines Proposal 1 for the Election of Directors, detailing voting rules and board composition. It features a table listing ten nominees for election to the Board of Directors, including their names, ages, tenure since joining, occupations, independence status, financial expertise, committee memberships, and other public board roles.

children.title: Proposal 1—Election of Directors
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors

children.title: Director Qualifications and Nomination of Directors
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Director Qualifications and Nomination of Directors
children.summary: This page outlines the qualifications and nomination process for directors at NVIDIA, managed by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC). It details specific criteria for evaluating nominees, such as integrity, independence, financial expertise, and experience in emerging technologies. The text also discusses the Board's strategy regarding refreshment to balance continuity with new perspectives, noting that one-third of independent directors have joined since 2020. This page outlines the skills, competencies, and attributes that the Board of Directors considers important for its members, covering areas such as senior leadership, industry expertise, financial experience, governance, emerging technologies, marketing, legal compliance, and human capital management. It also details the evaluation process for stockholder nominees by the NCGC (Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee) and explains the company's voluntary proxy access policy, which allows eligible stockholders to include director candidates in the company's proxy statement. This page, titled 'Our Director Nominees', presents detailed biographies for two director nominees: Tench Coxe and John O. Dabiri. For each individual, the document lists their age, tenure as a director, committee assignments, professional background, education, and specific areas of expertise relevant to the board.

children.title: Our Director Nominees
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees

children.title: Other Current Public Company Boards
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/Other Current Public Company Boards
children.summary: This page is a biographical profile of Jen-Hsun Huang, the President and Chief Executive Officer of NVIDIA Corporation. It details his career history, including founding NVIDIA in 1993, his previous work at LSI Logic and Advanced Micro Devices, and his educational background from Oregon State University and Stanford University. The text also lists his numerous awards, honorary degrees, and recognitions such as being named one of TIME magazine's 100 most influential people. A section at the bottom outlines his relevant experience categories, such as Senior Leadership, Industry & Technical expertise, and Governance.

children.title: DAWN HUDSON
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/DAWN HUDSON
children.summary: This document page (page 19) presents biographical summaries for two board members: Dawn Hudson and Harvey C. Jones. The section on Dawn Hudson details her extensive background as a former Chief Marketing Officer for the NFL and CEO of Pepsi-Cola North America, along with her various directorships at companies like P.F. Chang's and Amplify Snack Brands. The section on Harvey C. Jones outlines his career as an entrepreneur and Managing Partner of Square Wave Ventures, highlighting his experience in technology sectors including co-founding Daisy Systems Corp. and Synopsys, Inc.

children.title: HARVEY C. JONES
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/HARVEY C. JONES
children.summary: This section provides a professional biography of Harvey C. Jones, who is an Independent Director and Financial Expert on the board. It details his role as Managing Partner of Square Wave Ventures since 2004 and outlines his extensive career as an entrepreneur and high technology executive over the past 30 years. Key highlights include co-founding Daisy Systems Corp., leading Synopsys, Inc., and co-founding Tensilica Inc. The text also notes his educational background from Georgetown University and MIT, and emphasizes his expertise in semiconductor technologies, complex system design, and innovation strategies.

children.title: MELISSA B. LORA
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/MELISSA B. LORA
children.summary: This section details the professional background of Melissa B. Lora, a former President of Taco Bell International and Independent Director since 2023. It outlines her 31-year career at Taco Bell Corp., her board service with KB Home, Conagra Brands, Inc., and MGIC Investment Corporation, and her educational background from California State University-Long Beach and the University of Southern California. The section also highlights her key competencies in senior leadership, finance, governance, and brand management.

children.title: STEPHEN C. NEAL
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/STEPHEN C. NEAL
children.summary: This section provides a professional biography of Stephen C. Neal, who is 77 years old and has served as an Independent Director since 2019. He currently holds the titles of Chairman Emeritus and Senior Counsel at Cooley LLP, where he previously served as Chief Executive Officer from 2001 to 2008. The text details his extensive experience as a trial lawyer in corporate governance, his past partnership at Kirkland & Ellis LLP, and his service on the board of directors for Levi Strauss & Co. (2007-2021). Additionally, it mentions his role as Chairman of the Oversight Board Trust and previous chairmanships at the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation and the Monterey Bay Aquarium. Mr. Neal holds an AB degree from Harvard University and a JD from Stanford Law School.

children.title: A. BROOKE SEAWELL
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/A. BROOKE SEAWELL
children.summary: This section details the professional background and qualifications of A. Brooke Seawell, a Venture Partner at New Enterprise Associates and Independent Director since 1997. It outlines his extensive career in technology and finance, including roles at NetDynamics, Synopsys, and various board memberships (Tenable Holdings, Glu Mobile, Informatica, Tableau Software, Eargo). The text highlights his expertise in senior leadership, financial reporting, governance, and emerging technologies.

children.title: AARTI SHAH
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Proposal 1—Election of Directors/Our Director Nominees/AARTI SHAH
children.summary: This section details the professional background of Aarti Shah, a 61-year-old Independent Director who has served since 2020. It highlights her tenure as Former Senior Vice President & Chief Information and Digital Officer at Eli Lilly and Company, where she worked for 27 years. The text outlines her extensive board service with organizations such as Sandoz Group AG, Northwestern Mutual, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, and American Lebanese Syrian Associated Charities (ALSAC). Additionally, it notes her educational credentials, including a PhD in Applied Statistics from the University of California, Riverside.

children.title: Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance

children.title: Independence of the Members of the Board of Directors
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Independence of the Members of the Board of Directors
children.summary: This section outlines the requirements for director independence under Nasdaq rules and the company's Corporate Governance Policies. It states that, with the exception of Mr. Huang, all current and Fiscal 2026 directors are considered independent. Additionally, it confirms that members of the Audit Committee (AC), Compensation Committee (CC), and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC) are independent. The text further identifies Mr. Seawell, Mr. Jones, and Ms. Lora as 'audit committee financial experts' in compliance with SEC rules.

children.title: Board Leadership Structure
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Board Leadership Structure
children.summary: The 'Board Leadership Structure' section details NVIDIA's governance approach, which utilizes an independent Lead Director rather than a chairperson to ensure balanced oversight. The text outlines the rationale for this structure, emphasizing the active involvement of independent directors and the separation of management and board leadership roles. It identifies Stephen C. Neal as the current Lead Director (serving since 2019) and Chairperson of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC). The section further elaborates on Mr. Neal's qualifications, including his background as a trial attorney and executive experience, and lists specific duties such as setting meeting agendas, acting as a liaison between the CEO and independent directors, and presiding over meetings in the CEO's absence.

children.title: Committees of the Board of Directors
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Committees of the Board of Directors
children.summary: This page details the composition and responsibilities of the Audit Committee (AC) for the 2026 fiscal year. It lists five members, including Chairperson A. Brooke Seawell, and outlines their key duties such as overseeing financial reporting, internal audit functions, and the independent registered public accounting firm. The text also notes that the committee met four times in Fiscal 2026 to discuss topics like capitalization strategy, tax, and information security.

children.title: Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation
children.summary: The document page details the composition and responsibilities of two corporate committees: the Compensation Committee (CC) and the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC). For each committee, it lists the members as of the 2026 meeting, including their chairpersons, and outlines specific agenda topics discussed during Fiscal 2026. The page further elaborates on the distinct roles and responsibilities for both committees, such as executive compensation oversight for the CC and director candidate evaluation for the NCGC. A section at the bottom describes the interlocks and insider participation within the Compensation Committee.

children.title: Role of the Board in Risk Oversight
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Role of the Board in Risk Oversight
children.summary: This page details the 'Role of the Board in Risk Oversight' for NVIDIA. It features a comprehensive table titled 'RISK OVERSIGHT AT NVIDIA' that outlines the specific risk areas overseen by the full Board of Directors and its three main committees: the Audit Committee (AC), Compensation Committee (CC), and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC). The document also describes the roles of Management and Internal Audit in identifying, mitigating, and assuring internal controls.

children.title: Corporate Governance
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Corporate Governance
children.summary: This section details the Company's Corporate Governance framework, focusing on Board refreshment and policies. It highlights the appointment of Ms. Nora Johnson to the Board effective July 13, 2026, following an increase in board size from ten to eleven directors. The text outlines the NCGC's role in overseeing director evaluations, orientation, continuing education, and time commitments. Additionally, it specifies Director Stock Ownership Guidelines requiring non-employee directors to hold shares worth six times their annual cash retainer (or ten times base salary for the CEO) within five years of appointment. The section concludes by noting that senior management development is overseen by the CEO and that outside advisors may be retained at the Board's discretion.

children.title: Stockholder Communications with the Board of Directors
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Stockholder Communications with the Board of Directors
children.summary: This section outlines the procedure for stockholders to communicate with the Board of Directors regarding director nominations or other matters. Communications should be sent electronically to Timothy S. Teter, the Secretary, at shareholdermeeting@nvidia.com. The Secretary compiles these communications; if no specific director is named, letters are forwarded to the chairperson of the Audit Committee (AC), Compensation Committee (CC), or Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC). The NCGC reviews all such matters to determine if they should be presented to the full Board.

children.title: Majority Vote Standard
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Majority Vote Standard
children.summary: This section outlines the 'Majority Vote Standard' for director elections as defined in the company's Bylaws. It details that in uncontested elections, directors must receive a majority of votes cast (FOR exceeding AGAINST) to be elected; otherwise, they must tender their resignation, which is then reviewed by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (NCGC) and the Board within 90 days. In contested elections, directors are elected by a plurality of votes. The text also clarifies that abstentions and broker non-votes count towards quorum but do not affect the vote outcome.

children.title: Stockholder Special Meeting Right
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Stockholder Special Meeting Right
children.summary: The section details an amendment to the company's Bylaws in 2024, granting stockholders owning at least 15% of shares (held continuously for one year) the right to request a special meeting. It notes that requesters must meet specific disclosure and timing requirements to ensure adequate information is provided.

children.title: Board Meeting Information
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Board Meeting Information
children.summary: This section details the Board's meeting schedule and attendance for Fiscal 2026. It states that the Board met five times to discuss strategic direction, business opportunities, and product roadmaps. It also outlines the expectation for full attendance by Board members at all meetings of the Board and their respective committees, noting that each member attended 75% or more of applicable meetings during the fiscal year.

children.title: Corporate Sustainability
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Corporate Sustainability
children.summary: The section outlines NVIDIA's commitment to Corporate Sustainability (CS), emphasizing the integration of environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and governance into its business strategy. It details the oversight structure where the full Board holds ultimate responsibility, while specific committees like the NCGC and CSSC manage sustainability policies, risks, and strategies. The CS team reports semiannually to the NCGC and annually to the Board. Additionally, it highlights climate achievements in Fiscal 2025 (100% renewable energy usage) and new emission reduction targets for Fiscal 2030 validated by the Science Based Targets Initiative.

children.title: Public Policy Engagement and Accountability
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Information About the Board of Directors and Corporate Governance/Public Policy Engagement and Accountability
children.summary: This section outlines the company's public policy engagement and accountability measures. It states that the NCGC oversees these activities, which are conducted to advance the long-term interests of the Company and its stockholders. The text notes that U.S. federal lobbying activities are disclosed quarterly and publicly reported, the company belongs to trade associations worldwide, and management reports to the NCGC regarding policies and expenditures related to government relations.

children.title: Director Compensation

The CC also considers Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code to avoid adverse tax consequences. Additionally, it states that under ASC 718, the Company records share-based compensation expense over the vesting period.

The Board of Directors opposes this proposal and recommends shareholders vote against it. children.title: Proposal 5 – Report on Faith-Based Community Resource Groups
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors/Proposal 5 – Report on Faith-Based Community Resource Groups
children.summary: This section details a stockholder proposal requesting that NVIDIA's Board of Directors evaluate and report on the establishment of faith-based community resource groups (CRGs). The proponent argues that while NVIDIA supports other diversity-focused CRGs, it lacks one for religious groups despite its large, diverse workforce. The proposal cites concerns about religious discrimination and recent Supreme Court decisions to justify the request for an evaluation and risk assessment report. The Board opposes this proposal, recommending a vote against it, stating that existing policies and reporting mechanisms already adequately address issues related to religious discrimination and that the requested report is unnecessary.

children.title: Proposal 6 – Report on Respecting Workforce Civil Liberties
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors/Proposal 6 – Report on Respecting Workforce Civil Liberties
children.summary: This section details 'Proposal 6 – Report on Respecting Workforce Civil Liberties,' a stockholder proposal requesting an evaluation of NVIDIA's hiring and training policies regarding civil liberties. The proposal argues that current Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) practices are divisive and legally risky, citing recent Supreme Court decisions and executive orders. It requests a report on how these policies impact employees based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or political views. The Board of Directors opposes the proposal, recommending a vote against it, stating that NVIDIA already complies with applicable laws and has sufficient oversight mechanisms in place.

The document includes a supporting statement arguing that climate change poses macroeconomic risks and that NVIDIA's current disclosures are insufficient compared to peers like AMD, Intel, Onsemi, and NXP. It cites specific data points regarding climate disasters in 2025 and forecasts for AI energy demand.

children.title: The proposal is unnecessary given NVIDIA's history of robust climate reporting and targets, and our future disclosure plans
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors/Proposal 7 – Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosure/The proposal is unnecessary given NVIDIA's history of robust climate reporting and targets, and our future disclosure plans
children.summary: This section argues that the proposal is unnecessary because NVIDIA already demonstrates a strong commitment to sustainability and climate risk management. It highlights the company's detailed reporting in its 2025 Sustainability Report, which covers Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions across eight categories, as well as product energy efficiency and climate strategy. The text notes that new targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) were announced in 2025, including absolute reductions for Scope 1 and 2 and intensity reductions for Scope 3. Additionally, it mentions the publication of ISO-conformant, third-party reviewed product carbon footprints for accelerated computing products and plans to further enhance Scope 3 reporting.

children.title: The proposal adopts an overly prescriptive approach to highly complex disclosures
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/PROXY STATEMENT/Report of the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors/Proposal 7 – Greenhouse Gas Emissions Disclosure/The proposal adopts an overly prescriptive approach to highly complex disclosures
children.summary: This section argues that the proposal is overly prescriptive regarding complex Scope 3 emissions disclosures. It asserts that NVIDIA's management, supported by its CS team and overseen by the NCGC, is best positioned to determine the specific content and methodology of climate disclosures due to the inherent complexity and evolving nature of the AI computing industry. The text contends that a broad prescriptive mandate fails to acknowledge these challenges and is inappropriate given NVIDIA's track record.

children.title: Advancing the leading autonomous vehicle platform.

The company provides a comprehensive hardware and software solution under the DRIVE brand, designed from the ground up based on automotive safety standards. This solution includes GPU-based hardware for training neural networks and re-simulating operations prior to over-the-air updates. The strategy involves partnerships with various industry players including OEMs, mobility service providers, robotaxis, tier-1 suppliers, and start-ups.

children.summary: This page details various risk factors affecting the company's operations, including geopolitical instability in regions like China, Hong Kong, Israel, Korea, and Taiwan, as well as potential disruptions from natural disasters and third-party vendor failures. It specifically addresses the impact of the conflict in Israel on approximately 6,000 employees and discusses how climate change may adversely affect business through extreme weather events, particularly in Northern California where the Santa Clara headquarters is located. The text also outlines risks related to sustainability laws, carbon taxes, and supply chain governance.

children.title: We receive a significant amount of our revenue from a limited number of partners and distributors and we have a concentration of sales to customers who purchase directly or indirectly from us, and our revenue could be adversely affected if we lose or are prevented from selling to any of these customers.

Risk Factors/Risk Factors/We receive a significant amount of our revenue from a limited number of partners and distributors and we have a concentration of sales to customers who purchase directly or indirectly from us, and our revenue could be adversely affected if we lose or are prevented from selling to any of these customers.
children.summary: The section details the company's reliance on a limited number of partners, distributors, and direct customers for revenue. It highlights that sales to two specific direct customers accounted for 22% and 14% of total revenue in fiscal year 2026, primarily within the Compute & Networking segment. The text outlines risks associated with this concentration, including the potential for customers to cancel orders, develop their own solutions, or purchase from competitors. It also notes exposure to indirect customers (OEMs, ODMs, system integrators) who may represent significant portions of revenue and face credit limitations.

children.summary: The section discusses the counterparty risks associated with commercial arrangements, including long-term capacity purchase obligations and financial guarantees. It highlights that these arrangements expose the company to risks such as customers' or partners' inability to fulfill financial commitments, project delays, and financial distress or insolvency. Additionally, it notes that financing arrangements could result in lower upfront cash flows and increased credit risk.

children.title: If we are unable to attract, retain and motivate our executives and key employees, our business may be harmed.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/If we are unable to attract, retain and motivate our executives and key employees, our business may be harmed.
children.summary: This section outlines the risks associated with the company's inability to attract, retain, and motivate its executives and key employees. It highlights that labor is subject to external factors beyond the company's control, such as a highly competitive market for skilled workers, immigration regulations, and workforce participation rates. The text notes that competition for talent increases costs through cash and stock-based compensation, which may lose value during periods of stock price volatility. Furthermore, it emphasizes the high dependence on the current executive team and states that failure in succession planning or knowledge transfer could hinder strategic planning and long-term success.

children.title: Our business is dependent upon the proper functioning of our business processes and information systems and modification or interruption of such systems may disrupt our business and internal controls.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/Our business is dependent upon the proper functioning of our business processes and information systems and modification or interruption of such systems may disrupt our business and internal controls.
children.summary: The section discusses the company's reliance on internal processes and information systems, including ERP systems, to support business functions and comply with Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. It highlights risks associated with system modifications, implementation errors, or disruptions that could harm operations and financial reporting. Additionally, it addresses the potential negative impact of identifying material weaknesses in internal controls, which could lead to loss of investor confidence, stock price decline, restatement of financial statements, and regulatory sanctions.

children.title: Our operating results have in the past fluctuated and may in the future fluctuate, and if our operating results are below the expectations of securities analysts or investors, our stock price could decline.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/Our operating results have in the past fluctuated and may in the future fluctuate, and if our operating results are below the expectations of securities analysts or investors, our stock price could decline.
children.summary: This section warns that the company's operating results have fluctuated in the past and may continue to do so due to various factors, including multi-year product development cycles, contractual obligations, extended payment terms with customers, vendor payment requirements, environmental liabilities, and changes in accounting standards. It emphasizes that investors should not rely on past performance as an indicator of future results and notes that failure to meet expectations could lead to a decline in stock price.

children.title: We are subject to complex laws, rules, regulations, and political and other actions, including restrictions on the export of our products, which may adversely impact our business.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/We are subject to complex laws, rules, regulations, and political and other actions, including restrictions on the export of our products, which may adversely impact our business.
children.summary: This page details various risk factors affecting the company's business operations. It discusses the dependency on internal information systems and ERP implementations, the potential impact of material weaknesses in internal controls on financial reporting, and the volatility of operating results due to factors like product development cycles and payment terms. The final section outlines risks related to regulatory compliance, including laws regarding IP, taxes, anti-corruption (FCPA), data privacy, and cybersecurity. This page details the regulatory and compliance risks facing the company, particularly regarding antitrust legislation and AI regulations in major markets like the EU, US, UK, China, and South Korea. It discusses specific laws such as the EU AI Act and export control measures related to the war in Ukraine that have impacted sales in Russia and Belarus. The text highlights how government actions, including trade protectionism and sanctions, could restrict the company's ability to sell GPUs and other semiconductor products associated with AI. This page details the impact of U.S. export controls and economic sanctions on a company's business, specifically focusing on restrictions targeting GPUs, semiconductors, and AI technologies related to China. It outlines a timeline of regulatory changes from August 2022 through February 2026, including specific product bans (A100, H100, H20) and licensing requirements for exports to China and other countries. The text also highlights risks associated with antitrust investigations in China regarding the Mellanox acquisition. This page details the adverse business impacts of complex export controls and geopolitical tensions on a technology company's operations, particularly regarding sales in China. It discusses specific US government regulations like the AI Diffusion IFR and the GAIN AI Act, as well as restrictions on data center products (H200, GB200) and gaming GPUs. The text highlights how these rules have foreclosed market access, harmed competitive positions against rivals, and introduced risks related to licensing requirements and potential vulnerabilities in chip designs.

children.title: Scrutiny from shareholders, regulators and others regarding our corporate sustainability practices could result in additional costs or risks and adversely impact our reputation and willingness of customers and suppliers to do business with us.

It discusses how restrictions on selling GPUs to markets like China, Europe, and Southeast Asia could disrupt supply chains and reduce demand for data center products. The text also highlights potential negative impacts from Chinese government policies on gaming revenue and data center adoption, as well as scrutiny regarding corporate sustainability practices.

children.title: Issues relating to the responsible use of our technologies, including AI in our offerings, may result in reputational or financial harm and liability.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/Issues relating to the responsible use of our technologies, including AI in our offerings, may result in reputational or financial harm and liability.
children.summary: This section discusses the risks associated with the responsible use of new and evolving technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI). It highlights that AI applications can pose legal, social, and ethical issues, including unintended consequences, copyright infringement, and impacts on human rights or privacy. The text notes that failure to implement effective internal policies or comply with regulations—such as those in the European Union regarding General Purpose Artificial Intelligence—could lead to reputational harm, financial costs, and reduced public confidence.

children.title: Actions to adequately protect our IP rights could result in substantial costs to us and our ability to compete could be harmed if we are unsuccessful or if we are prohibited from making or selling our products.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/Actions to adequately protect our IP rights could result in substantial costs to us and our ability to compete could be harmed if we are unsuccessful or if we are prohibited from making or selling our products.
children.summary: This section outlines the risks associated with intellectual property (IP) rights. It details potential costs and competitive harms arising from legal proceedings, including lawsuits alleging patent infringement or other IP violations. The text explains that unfavorable rulings could lead to significant damages, invalidation of patents, or injunctions. Conversely, initiating legal action to protect IP can increase operating expenses and expose the company to countersuits. Additionally, it highlights the challenges of protecting IP in foreign jurisdictions where laws may be less robust than in the United States, increasing the risk of piracy, theft of trade secrets, and unauthorized use by competitors.

children.title: We may have exposure to additional tax liabilities and our operating results may be adversely impacted by changes in tax laws, higher than expected tax rates and other tax-related factors.
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part I/Item 1A. Risk Factors/Risk Factors/We may have exposure to additional tax liabilities and our operating results may be adversely impacted by changes in tax laws, higher than expected tax rates and other tax-related factors.
children.summary: The section discusses the company's exposure to additional tax liabilities and potential adverse impacts from changes in tax laws, higher tax rates, and other tax-related factors. It highlights that the company is subject to complex income and non-income-based taxes globally and is regularly under audit. Key risks include increases in the worldwide effective tax rate due to U.S. tax law changes (such as reductions in FDDEI deductions) or international developments like the OECD Two-Pillar framework. The text also notes that future effective tax rates may be affected by business mix, statutory rate changes, accounting principles, stock-based compensation volatility, and deferred tax asset valuation.

children.summary: This section outlines the company's exposure to legal, administrative, and regulatory proceedings, including claims related to shareholders, consumers, competition, and intellectual property. It specifically mentions a securities class action lawsuit regarding false or misleading statements about cryptocurrency mining and GPU demand in 2017 and 2018. The text highlights that litigation is inherently uncertain and could result in monetary damages, fines, injunctions, or other remedies, which would be costly, time-consuming, and disruptive.

It includes a table detailing the Name, Title, Action (Adoption), Date, Total Shares of Common Stock to be Sold, and Expiration Date for John O. Dabiri and Colette M. Kress.

children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part II/Item 9C. Disclosure Regarding Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections

Directors, Executive Officers and Corporate Governance', states that information regarding directors is incorporated by reference from the company's 2026 Proxy Statement under the caption 'Proposal 1 — Election of Directors'. Additionally, information regarding executive officers is incorporated by reference from Part I of the Annual Report on Form 10-K under the heading 'Information About Our Executive Officers'.

children.title: Item 11. Executive Compensation
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part III/Item 11. Executive Compensation
children.summary: This section states that information regarding executive compensation will be contained in the company's 2026 Proxy Statement under specific captions, including 'Executive Compensation,' 'Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation,' 'Director Compensation,' and 'Compensation Committee Report.' The content is incorporated by reference.

children.summary: This section, titled 'Item 12. Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder Matters', states that information regarding the ownership of NVIDIA securities will be contained in the company's 2026 Proxy Statement under the caption 'Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management'. children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part III/Item 13. Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence

children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part III/Item 14. Principal Accountant Fees and Services
children.summary: This section states that information regarding accounting fees and services required by Item 14 will be contained in the company's 2026 Proxy Statement under the caption "Fees Billed by the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm," and is hereby incorporated by reference.

children.title: Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules
