children.title: Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting

children.title: Basis for Opinions
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting/Basis for Opinions
children.summary: This section outlines the responsibilities of management versus the independent registered public accounting firm regarding the consolidated financial statements and internal control over financial reporting. It details that the audits were conducted in accordance with Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) standards to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement and if effective internal controls were maintained. The text describes the audit procedures performed, including risk assessment, testing evidence on a sample basis, evaluating accounting principles and estimates, and assessing the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls.

children.title: Definition and Limitations of Internal Control over Financial Reporting
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting/Definition and Limitations of Internal Control over Financial Reporting
children.summary: This section defines internal control over financial reporting as a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. It details that this control includes policies and procedures for maintaining accurate records, ensuring authorized transactions, and preventing unauthorized asset acquisition or use. The text also outlines inherent limitations, noting that controls may not prevent all misstatements and that future projections of effectiveness are subject to risks such as changing conditions or deteriorating compliance.

children.title: Critical Audit Matters
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Critical Audit Matters
children.summary: This section details the critical audit matter concerning the valuation of inventories, specifically focusing on provisions for excess or obsolete inventories and excess product purchase commitments. It explains that this area required significant judgment from management regarding future demand and market conditions, which in turn necessitated substantial auditor effort to evaluate these assumptions. The text provides context by stating the company's consolidated inventory balance was $21.4 billion as of January 25, 2026. It also outlines the procedures performed by the auditors, including testing controls, evaluating management's process and approach, and assessing the reasonableness of assumptions related to historical results, external data, and technology changes.

children.title: Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies

children.title: Our Company
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Our Company
children.summary: The section titled 'Our Company' describes NVIDIA's corporate history and structure. It states that the company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, was incorporated in California in April 1993, and reincorporated in Delaware in April 1998. It also defines the scope of references to 'NVIDIA', 'we', 'us', 'our', or 'the Company' as including NVIDIA Corporation and its subsidiaries.

children.title: Fiscal Year
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Fiscal Year
children.summary: The section describes NVIDIA's fiscal year structure, noting that the company operates on a 52- or 53-week year ending on the last Sunday in January. It specifies that fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024 were all 52-week years, while fiscal year 2027 will be a 53-week year with the fourth quarter consisting of 14 weeks.

children.title: Principles of Consolidation
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Principles of Consolidation
children.summary: The section outlines the scope of NVIDIA's consolidated financial statements, stating they include the accounts of NVIDIA Corporation and its wholly-owned subsidiaries. It further specifies that all intercompany balances and transactions are eliminated during consolidation.

children.title: Use of Estimates
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Use of Estimates
children.summary: The 'Use of Estimates' section explains that preparing financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions affecting reported assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. It details the ongoing evaluation of these estimates regarding accounts receivable, cash equivalents, marketable securities, goodwill, income taxes, inventories, product purchase commitments, litigation, and stock-based compensation.

children.title: Revenue Recognition
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition

children.title: Product Sales Revenue
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Product Sales Revenue
children.summary: This section details the accounting policies for recognizing revenue from product sales. It explains that revenue is recognized upon transfer of control and reflects the expected consideration. The text covers specific scenarios including support and extended warranty services (recognized ratably), products with a right of return (requiring a sales return allowance based on historical rates), and customer programs involving rebates and MDFs (accounted for as reductions to revenue).

children.title: Contracts with Multiple Performance Obligations
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Contracts with Multiple Performance Obligations
children.summary: This section outlines the accounting policy for contracts containing multiple deliverables. It explains that distinct performance obligations are accounted for separately and that total transaction prices are allocated based on relative standalone selling prices, maximizing the use of observable inputs.

children.title: Product Warranties
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Product Warranties
children.summary: The section describes the company's limited warranty policy for end-users, covering a period of one to three years for manufacturing defects or hardware failures. It explains that revenue costs include estimated warranty expenses calculated at the point of revenue recognition and mentions accruals for known warranty issues when probable and estimable.

children.title: Stock-based Compensation
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Stock-based Compensation
children.summary: The section details the accounting policies for stock-based compensation. It explains that the fair value of restricted stock units (RSUs) is based on the closing trading price of common stock, while performance stock units (PSUs) are valued using a Monte Carlo simulation. The text outlines the amortization methods used for expense recognition: straight-line for RSUs and market-based PSUs, and an accelerated model for PSUs based on probable achievement of targets. Additionally, it describes the use of the Black-Scholes model to estimate the fair value of shares under the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) and notes that expected forfeitures are estimated based on historical data.

children.title: Litigation, Investigation and Settlement Costs
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Litigation, Investigation and Settlement Costs
children.summary: The section outlines the company's exposure to various claims, litigation, and investigations, including patent disputes, antitrust matters, and employment issues. It details the accounting policy for recording losses when they are probable and reasonably estimable, while noting that actual liabilities may differ from estimates.

children.title: Foreign Currency Remeasurement
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Foreign Currency Remeasurement
children.summary: This section outlines the company's accounting policy for foreign currency remeasurement. It states that the U.S. dollar is the functional currency for subsidiaries. Monetary assets and liabilities are remeasured at end-of-period exchange rates, while non-monetary items like property and equipment are remeasured at historical rates. Revenue and expenses are generally remeasured at current period rates, with exceptions for certain balance sheet-related expenses. The text notes that gains or losses from this process have not been significant to date.

children.title: Income Taxes
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Revenue Recognition/Income Taxes
children.summary: The section outlines the company's accounting policies for income taxes, specifically regarding the recognition of federal, state, and foreign current tax liabilities or assets based on estimated taxes payable or refundable. It also details the recognition of deferred tax assets and liabilities based on estimates of future tax effects from temporary differences and carryforwards, including the use of valuation allowances to reduce deferred tax assets that are not expected to be realized.

children.title: Net Income Per Share
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Net Income Per Share
children.summary: This section outlines the methodology for calculating basic and diluted net income per share. Basic net income per share is computed using the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net income per share uses the weighted average number of common and potentially dilutive shares, applying the treasury stock method. It also notes that anti-dilutive equity awards are excluded from the diluted calculation.

children.title: Cash and Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Cash and Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities
children.summary: This section defines cash equivalents as highly liquid investments with an original maturity of three months or less, and marketable securities as debt investments with maturities greater than three months and publicly-held equity securities. It details the accounting treatment for these assets, noting that available-for-sale debt securities are reported at fair value with unrealized gains/losses in accumulated other comprehensive income. The text also covers impairment reviews for debt securities, the specific-identification method for realized gains/losses on sales, and the reporting of changes in fair value for equity securities and money market funds.

children.title: Fair Value of Financial Instruments
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Fair Value of Financial Instruments
children.summary: This section details the accounting policies for determining fair value. It states that carrying values of cash equivalents, receivables, and payables approximate their fair value due to short maturities as of January 25, 2026, and January 26, 2025. Marketable debt and equity securities are reported at fair value, while derivative instruments are recognized as assets or liabilities measured at fair value. The text outlines how changes in fair value are recorded depending on whether derivatives are designated as accounting hedges. Finally, it introduces a classification system based on the observability of inputs used to determine fair value, defining Level 1 (observable inputs like quoted prices) and Level 2 (observable inputs other than Level 1).

children.title: Concentration of Credit Risk
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Concentration of Credit Risk
children.summary: This section outlines the financial instruments subject to credit risk, primarily cash equivalents, marketable securities, lease guarantees, and accounts receivable. It details the company's investment policy focusing on high-rated fixed income securities and diversification. The text also describes the process for ongoing credit evaluations of customers and the maintenance of an allowance for potential credit losses, which covers specific customer amounts and overall estimated exposure excluding insurance-covered amounts.

children.title: Inventories
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Inventories
children.summary: The 'Inventories' section details the accounting policy for inventory cost computation, which is based on an adjusted standard basis approximating actual cost (average or FIFO). It outlines that costs include semiconductors, manufacturing support, and purchased components. The company records provisions to write down inventory to its lower of cost or net realizable value for obsolete, excess, or non-cancelable purchase commitments.

children.title: Property and Equipment
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Property and Equipment
children.summary: The 'Property and Equipment' section details the accounting policies for these assets, stating they are recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation. Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line method over estimated useful lives of two to seven years (buildings up to thirty years). It also covers the removal of retired assets, the inclusion of amortization from finance leases in depreciation expense, and the amortization of leasehold improvements.

children.title: Leases
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Leases
children.summary: This section outlines the company's accounting policy for leases. It details how arrangements are identified as leases at inception and describes the recognition of operating lease assets and liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet. The text explains that these assets and liabilities are based on the present value of remaining lease payments discounted using the incremental borrowing rate, including initial direct costs and prepaid payments. Lease costs are recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term.

children.title: Goodwill
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Goodwill
children.summary: The section outlines the company's policy for allocating goodwill to reporting units based on expected benefits from business combinations. It details that goodwill is subject to an annual impairment test conducted in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year, or earlier if impairment indicators exist. The company performs either a qualitative or quantitative analysis for this test, considering factors such as industry and market conditions, financial performance, and other relevant events. The text notes that no goodwill impairments were identified for the periods presented.

children.title: Intangible Assets and Other Long-Lived Assets
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Intangible Assets and Other Long-Lived Assets
children.summary: This section details the company's accounting policies for intangible assets and other long-lived assets. It specifies that intangible assets primarily consist of acquired developed technology, customer relationships, and rights under technology licenses, patents, and acquired IP. The company amortizes these finite-life assets over periods ranging from one to twenty years using a method that reflects the pattern in which the economic benefits are consumed.

children.title: Business Combination
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Business Combination
children.summary: The section details the Company's accounting policy for business combinations. It describes a screen test used to distinguish between asset acquisitions and business combinations. For business combinations, the purchase price is allocated to tangible assets, liabilities assumed, and intangible assets based on fair value, with any excess recorded as goodwill. The text highlights that these valuations rely on management estimates regarding future cash flows and discount rates, which are subject to uncertainty. Adjustments to the purchase price allocation may be made within one year of the acquisition date, affecting goodwill or income. Additionally, it states that acquisition-related expenses are expensed as incurred.

children.title: Non-Marketable Equity Securities
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Non-Marketable Equity Securities
children.summary: This section outlines the accounting policy for non-marketable equity securities, which are investments in privately-held companies without readily determinable fair values. These securities are measured at cost minus impairment or using the measurement alternative based on observable price changes. The company assesses these investments for significant influence to determine if the equity method applies, noting that such investments were not material.

children.title: Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 1 - Organization and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies/Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements
children.summary: This section details a new accounting standard issued by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) in November 2024. The standard requires additional annual and interim disclosures regarding specific expense items, including inventory purchases, employee compensation, depreciation, and intangible asset amortization. The company plans to adopt this standard for its fiscal year 2028 annual report and does not expect it to have a material impact on its financial statements beyond these additional disclosures.

children.title: Note 2 - Groq
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 2 - Groq
children.summary: This section details a non-exclusive license agreement entered into by NVIDIA with Groq, Inc. in December 2025 for language processing unit technology and the hiring of certain employees. The transaction involved recording $14.4 billion in goodwill and a $2.5 billion developed technology intangible asset. Total consideration consisted of $13.0 billion paid at closing and $4 billion payable within one year.

children.title: Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation
children.summary: This section details NVIDIA's stock-based compensation policies and financial data. It outlines the types of equity awards recognized, including Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), Performance Stock Units (PSUs), market-based PSUs, and issuances under the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). The content includes two tables: one breaking down stock-based compensation expense by category (Cost of revenue, Research and development, Sales, general and administrative) for the years ended Jan 25, 2026, Jan 26, 2025, and Jan 28, 2024; and another summarizing equity awards granted, showing metrics like awards granted, estimated total grant-date fair value, and weighted average grant-date fair value per share for RSUs/PSUs and ESPP shares purchased. The section concludes with a statement regarding aggregate unearned stock-based compensation expense as of January 25, 2026.

children.title: ESPP
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation/ESPP
children.summary: This section details the assumptions used to estimate the fair value of shares issued under the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) for the years ended January 25, 2026, January 26, 2025, and January 28, 2024. It includes a table presenting data on weighted average expected life, risk-free interest rate, volatility, and dividend yield based on the Black-Scholes model. The text explains that the expected term represents the period from the offering start to the purchase date, volatility is estimated using historical data, and dividend yield is applied at the grant date.

children.title: Equity Incentive Program
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation/Equity Incentive Program

children.title: Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation/Equity Incentive Program/Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan
children.summary: The section details the Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan (the '2007 Plan'), which authorizes the issuance of various stock-based awards including incentive stock options, RSUs, PSUs, and performance cash awards to employees, directors, and consultants. It specifies that as of January 25, 2026, up to 192 million shares were available for issuance under this plan. The text also outlines vesting schedules: RSUs generally vest over four years subject to service, while Performance Stock Units (PSUs) vest over four years based on service and performance conditions, and market-based PSUs vest approximately three years after grant subject to market conditions.

children.title: Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation/Equity Incentive Program/Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
children.summary: This section outlines the terms of the NVIDIA Corporation Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the 2012 Plan). It specifies that participating employees may have up to 25% of their earnings withheld to purchase common stock, with offering periods lasting approximately 24 months. The purchase price is set at 85% of the lower of the fair market value on the commencement date or each purchase date. As of January 25, 2026, 2.2 billion shares were reserved for future issuance under this plan.

children.title: Equity Award Activity
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation/Equity Award Activity
children.summary: The section titled 'Equity Award Activity' provides a summary of equity award transactions under NVIDIA's equity incentive plans. It includes a table detailing the activity for RSUs, PSUs, and Market-based PSUs outstanding, showing the number of shares and weighted average grant-date fair value per share for balances as of Jan 26, 2025, and Jan 25, 2026, along with granted, vested, and canceled/forfeited amounts. The text also notes the number of common stock shares available for future grants and reports the total fair value of RSUs and PSUs vesting during fiscal years 2024, 2025, and 2026.

children.title: Note 4 - Net Income Per Share
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 4 - Net Income Per Share
children.summary: This section presents the basic and diluted net income per share computations for NVIDIA Corporation for the years ended January 25, 2026, January 26, 2025, and January 28, 2024. The table details the numerator (Net Income) and denominator components (Basic weighted average shares, Dilutive impact of outstanding equity awards, and Diluted weighted average shares). It concludes with the calculated Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share values and lists anti-dilutive equity awards excluded from the calculation.

children.title: Note 5 - Goodwill
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 5 - Goodwill
children.summary: This section details the carrying amount of goodwill for NVIDIA Corporation as of January 25, 2026 ($20.8 billion) and January 26, 2025 ($5.2 billion), broken down by reporting units (Compute & Networking and Graphics). It notes a $15.6 billion increase in fiscal year 2026 allocated to the Compute & Networking unit and confirms that no impairment was identified during annual qualitative tests for fiscal years 2024, 2025, and 2026.

children.title: Note 6 - Amortizable Intangible Assets
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 6 - Amortizable Intangible Assets
children.summary: This page, titled 'Note 6 - Amortizable Intangible Assets' from NVIDIA Corporation's financial statements, details the components of amortizable intangible assets as of January 25, 2026, and January 26, 2025. The first table breaks down these assets into 'Acquisition-related intangible assets' and 'Patents and licensed technology,' listing their gross carrying amounts, accumulated amortization, and net carrying amounts in millions. A second table outlines the estimated future amortization expense for fiscal years 2027 through 2032 and thereafter.

children.title: Note 7 - Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 7 - Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities
children.summary: This page presents Note 7 from NVIDIA Corporation's Consolidated Financial Statements, detailing the fair values of cash equivalents and marketable securities as of January 25, 2026. The content is dominated by a comprehensive table categorizing financial assets into pricing levels (Level 1 and Level 2) and listing their cost, unrealized gains/losses, and estimated fair value. The table breaks down holdings such as U.S. Treasury debt, corporate debt, government agency bonds, certificates of deposit, foreign government bonds, money market funds, and publicly-held equity securities, further classifying them as Cash Equivalents, Marketable Securities, or Other Assets.

children.title: Note 8 - Non-marketable Equity Securities
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 8 - Non-marketable Equity Securities
children.summary: This page from NVIDIA Corporation's financial statements details the fair value hierarchy of its debt and equity securities as of January 26, 2025. It includes a table breaking down assets by pricing category (Level 1 and Level 2) and classifying them into cash equivalents or marketable securities. Additionally, it provides tables showing unrealized losses on debt securities categorized by duration and contractual maturity dates.

children.title: Note 9 - Balance Sheet Components
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 9 - Balance Sheet Components
children.summary: This section details the changes in short- and long-term deferred revenue for fiscal years 2026 and 2025. It presents a table showing the balance at the beginning of the period, deferred revenue additions (including customer advances), revenue recognized, and the balance at the end of the period. Footnotes clarify that these figures include amounts related to hardware, software support, cloud services, and license arrangements.

children.title: Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments

children.title: Foreign Currency Derivatives
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments/Foreign Currency Derivatives
children.summary: The section details the use of foreign currency forward contracts to mitigate exchange rate risks on operating expenses and monetary assets/liabilities. It explains that contracts for operating expenses are designated as accounting hedges, while those for assets and liabilities are not. A table presents the notional value of these outstanding contracts as of January 25, 2026 ($1,765 million designated, $2,332 million not designated) and January 26, 2025 ($1,424 million designated, $1,297 million not designated). The text notes that unrealized gains/losses were not significant and all contracts mature within 18 months.

children.title: Facility Lease Guarantees
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments/Facility Lease Guarantees
children.summary: This section details agreements entered into during fiscal year 2026 to guarantee partners' facility lease obligations in exchange for warrants. It specifies a maximum gross exposure of $3.5 billion, which is reduced as partners make payments over terms ranging from 5 to 7 years. Additionally, it notes that partners have placed $712 million in escrow to mitigate potential exposure and states that the guarantees, classified as credit derivatives, were not material.

children.title: Note 11 - Debt
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 11 - Debt
children.summary: This section details NVIDIA's debt obligations as of January 25, 2026, and January 26, 2025. It includes a table listing various notes due between 2026 and 2060, showing their expected remaining terms, effective interest rates, and carrying amounts in millions. The text further explains that the notes are unsecured senior obligations with semi-annual interest payments, outlines compliance with non-financial covenants, and mentions an increase in the commercial paper program size to $25.0 billion.

children.title: Note 12 - Commitments and Contingencies

children.title: Commitments
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 12 - Commitments and Contingencies/Commitments
children.summary: This section details NVIDIA's financial commitments as of January 25, 2026. It outlines manufacturing and supply commitments totaling $95.2 billion, multi-year cloud service agreement commitments of $27 billion with specific payment schedules through fiscal year 2032, investment commitments of $11.4 billion, and other commitments of $3.4 billion.

children.title: Accrual for Product Warranty Liabilities
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 12 - Commitments and Contingencies/Accrual for Product Warranty Liabilities
children.summary: This section details the estimated product warranty liabilities for NVIDIA Corporation as of January 25, 2026 ($2.8 billion) and January 26, 2025 ($1.3 billion). It includes a table showing the activity for the years ended Jan 25, 2026, Jan 26, 2025, and Jan 28, 2024, covering balances at the beginning and end of periods, additions, and utilization (in millions). The text notes that additions primarily related to the Compute & Networking segment. Additionally, it mentions indemnities provided for tax, product, and employee liabilities, noting that maximum potential future payments cannot be estimated.

children.title: Litigation
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 12 - Commitments and Contingencies/Litigation
children.summary: This section details the status of securities class action and derivative lawsuits against NVIDIA Corporation. It describes a putative securities class action (In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation) filed in 2018 alleging violations of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 regarding channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining impacts. The text outlines the procedural history, including the initial dismissal, appeals to the Ninth Circuit, and subsequent Supreme Court involvement, noting that the case was remanded to the district court for further proceedings as of early 2025. Additionally, it covers pending derivative lawsuits in the Northern District of California and Delaware, which are stayed pending the resolution of the securities litigation.

children.title: Accounting for Loss Contingencies
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 12 - Commitments and Contingencies/Accounting for Loss Contingencies
children.summary: The section titled 'Accounting for Loss Contingencies' states that as of January 25, 2026, the company has not accrued any contingent liabilities related to the legal proceedings described in the preceding text. This is because the company believes that while liabilities are reasonably possible, they are not probable, and any potential loss cannot be reasonably estimated at this time. The company also notes it is engaged in other ordinary course business legal actions and inquiries, which could have a material adverse effect on its financial position if outcomes are unfavorable.

children.title: Note 13 - Income Taxes
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 13 - Income Taxes
children.summary: This section details NVIDIA Corporation's income tax disclosures for fiscal years 2024, 2025, and 2026. It includes tables breaking down income tax expense into current and deferred components (Federal, State, Foreign), a reconciliation of the effective tax rate to the U.S. federal statutory rate, and a schedule of cash paid for income taxes. The note also presents the significant temporary differences giving rise to deferred tax assets and liabilities, discusses valuation allowances, and outlines net operating loss carryforwards and research tax credit carryforwards.

children.title: Note 14 - Shareholders' Equity
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 14 - Shareholders' Equity
children.summary: This section details the Capital Return Program, including a share repurchase authorization of $60.0 billion approved on August 26, 2025. It reports that 282 million shares were repurchased for $40.4 billion in fiscal year 2026 and 310 million shares for $34.0 billion in fiscal year 2025. Additionally, cash dividends paid to shareholders amounted to $974 million, $834 million, and $395 million for fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.

children.title: Note 15 - Employee Retirement Plans
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 15 - Employee Retirement Plans
children.summary: This section details the company's tax-qualified defined contribution plans for eligible employees in the U.S. and other countries. It reports the contribution expenses incurred for fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024.

children.title: Note 16 - Segment Information
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 16 - Segment Information
children.summary: This section details NVIDIA's reportable segments: Compute & Networking and Graphics. It defines the scope of each segment, explains that certain expenses are not allocated to segments for decision-making purposes, and provides financial data tables showing revenue, other segment items, and operating income for fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024. The section also includes a reconciliation of segment operating income to consolidated income before tax, geographic revenue breakdowns based on customer headquarters, and information regarding significant direct customers.

children.title: Note 17 - Leases
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules/Note 17 - Leases
children.summary: This section details NVIDIA's lease obligations, primarily operating leases for offices and data centers. It presents a table of future minimum non-cancelable lease payments by fiscal year, totaling $3,624 million, which is adjusted for imputed interest to determine the present value of net future minimum lease payments ($2,944 million). The section also provides supplemental cash flow information related to leases and notes on weighted average remaining lease terms and discount rates.

children.title: Item 16. Form 10-K Summary
children.path: NVIDIA FY26 Annual Report.pdf/Part IV/Item 16. Form 10-K Summary
children.summary: This page is an index of exhibits and documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), likely as part of a Form 10-K Annual Report. It lists various corporate plans, certifications, and XBRL data files, including the 'Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan' and the 'NVIDIA Corporation Insider Trading Policy'. The document also includes footnotes explaining filing statuses and provides contact information for Investor Relations at NVIDIA Corporation.

children.title: Signatures

children.summary: This section contains the formal signatures and a Power of Attorney for NVIDIA Corporation's report, dated February 25, 2026. Kress, Donald Robertson, and several directors) with their respective titles and the date of signing.
